text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High error rate on streaming-decode-prod (gpu-decode pool). Observed CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Paging oncall: tina_oncall.

alex k: seeing lots of dropped requests and 500s reported from the API gateway. Customer reports of truncated responses.

maria (sre): confirmed logs show repeated "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" during decode for long-running streams. Looks correlated with requests where client-side max_tokens is very large (or absent).

raj (runtime): probable runaway generation + no token cap. Our runtime currently allows streaming requests to specify max_tokens; if omitted we default to model limit. That combination with prefix caching can blow GPU mem.

alex k: can we temporarily enforce a server-side cap while we triage? even 1024 would help.

eng-runtime-bot: Suggested mitigation rule ready: set per-request max_tokens hard-cap to 1024 for streaming-decode-prod, and enable quick fallback to cpu-decode for large sequences.

tina_oncall: I'm on it. Will coordinate with runtime to push hotfix and then scale down affected nodes.

maria (sre): note: a few nodes are flapping (OOM -> kube crashloop -> restart) which is causing routing jitter and more pressure on remaining GPUs. We should cordon the noisy nodes asap to stop churn.

raj (runtime): agreed. Plan: 1) apply hotfix to enforce max_tokens cap at the routing layer; 2) add a temporary throttle rule that rejects streaming calls without max_tokens with a 429 and an explanatory error; 3) cordon noisy nodes; 4) enable CPU fallback path for queued requests to avoid total drops.

alex k: put the exact commands you want and I'll run via runway.

raj (runtime): run these steps in order — commands below.

```
# 1) apply routing cap
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/v1/overrides
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN"
  -d '{"service":"streaming-decode-prod","enforce_max_tokens":1024,"reject_if_missing_max_tokens":true}'

# 2) cordon noisy nodes
kubectl get pods -n decode-prod -o wide | grep OOM | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -I{} kubectl annotate pod {} maintenance=true

# 3) enable cpu fallback rollout
kubectl -n decode-prod set env deploy/runtime-service USE_CPU_FALLBACK=true --record
```

maria (sre): I'll cordon pods at the infra level (taints) so scheduler stops placing new workloads on the noisy nodes.

customer-success-john: Heads up — customer #ACME reported 30% of streaming requests failed starting ~16:45 UTC. They're asking for an incident summary and ETA to recovery.

tina_oncall: acknowledged. Please capture the customer impact window and list affected models.

eng-runtime-bot: quick check: models running on gpu-decode pool: gpt-small-decoder-v1, llama-stream-13b, redwood-rl-decoder. Llama instances had the highest token lengths.

raj (runtime): rolling the routing cap now. Pushing config...

incident-bot: Config override applied by raj (runtime) at 2371001299. Rule id: cfg-5902.

alex k: I'm seeing immediate drop in OOM rate on the control plane logs. Error surface is now 429 for those large streaming attempts (expected).

maria (sre): cordoning noisy nodes: marking 3 pods tainted and scaling down their replica set to avoid immediate reschedule.

raj (runtime): enabling CPU fallback environment...

incident-bot: CPU fallback toggle set to true at 2371001420. Fallback engages for queued requests that exceed GPU memory budget.

tina_oncall: monitoring customer traffic. Are we able to replay any in-flight requests to CPU fallback or do they have to be retried client-side?

raj (runtime): in-flight streams that were cut are returned with a retriable error code and hint header: X-RI-Retry: true. Gateway will retry once to CPU fallback if enabled. We'll monitor retry rate to ensure we don't overload CPU cluster.

alex k: small patch to gateway to add an explanatory message to 429: "Request rejected: server-enforced max_tokens=1024. Please set max_tokens or contact support."

customer-success-john: letting ACME know we've applied a temporary cap and have a plan. Requesting ETA to full restore.

maria (sre): immediate ETA: stabilize in 15-30m after cordon + fallback. Full restore (remove caps) after root cause and safe limits validated — likely a few hours.

raj (runtime): quick postmortem notes: root cause appears to be clients sending large or unbounded generation requests while a new weight cache policy increased per-request KV usage; combined it pushed some shard memory over threshold. We'll add guardrails: server-side caps, adaptive KV eviction, and better model mem profiling.

alex k: are we seeing any customer errors beyond ACME? any security/PII exposure?

maria (sre): no evidence of data leakage. It's an availability incident only.

tina_oncall: handoff: I'm staying on until system stabilizes. If anything spikes again, page me. I'll document timeline and actions for postmortem.

raj (runtime): will follow up with a hotfix PR to default max_tokens at the runtime API and add telemetry to count unbounded requests.

eng-runtime-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/467 — adds server-side default cap + metrics.

customer-success-john: ACME acknowledged mitigation and appreciates proactive updates. Asking for a short summary for SL.

maria (sre): summary to send: 1) incident started at 16:44 UTC with elevated CUDA OOMs causing node restarts and request drops; 2) immediate mitigations: enforced server-side max_tokens=1024, cordoned noisy nodes, enabled CPU fallback; 3) status: traffic stable, error rate dropped to baseline; 4) next steps: root cause analysis, revert caps when safe, improve guardrails.

alex k: logs/trace snippets saved to /incidents/2371001234/artifacts for postmortem.

tina_oncall: handing off to maria for postmortem write-up. I'll remain available for clarifying questions.

maria (sre): Acknowledged. Creating postmortem draft and will include timeline and customer impact. Closing thread when final doc posted. :white_check_mark:
